source_artifacts.locator: approval card (as shown to the clerk)

capabilities.target: ERP vendor master record, including bank details
ERP vendor master bank detail field
Outbound payment to vendor bank account on file

inputs.source: Supplier invoice uploaded to the supplier portal

instructions.note: The instruction unconditionally authorizes updating vendor bank details whenever 'the invoice shows new bank details,' treating untrusted invoice content as sufficient authority to change payment-destination master data, with no independent verification step specified.
No limit is stated on which vendors, amounts, or invoice volumes the agent may process; combined with a broad ERP credential, a single compromised invoice can redirect payment for any vendor.

elements.name: Outbound payment execution to vendor bank account

controls.name: Clerk approval card before payment or bank change
controls.decay_rationale: The gate blocks execution pending a human click, but the decision rests entirely on a one-line model-generated summary that never shows the bank account number or change history. A more persuasive or more capable model can write a summary that reads as routine even when the underlying action is fraudulent (ASI09), and the review surface does not scale to show more as the model improves.

controls.name: Out-of-band verification of vendor bank-detail changes bound to the system of record
controls.decay_rationale: Verification against a contact number already on file (not one supplied by the invoice) is enforced outside the model and does not depend on model behavior to work.

controls.name: Approval card shows raw destination (bank account reference) and change history, not just a summary
Scope the ERP credential away from blanket any-vendor, any-amount access
Anomaly detection on vendor bank-detail changes followed closely by a payment request
controls.decay_rationale: A classifier trained on normal change patterns can be evaded by a sufficiently tailored invoice, though it still raises the bar independent of the agent's own model.

controls.name: Aggregate spend/rate/step cap on payment scheduling and bank-detail changes

findings.title: Summary-gated approval lets a spoofed invoice redirect vendor payments (TC9 + vendor-master poisoning)

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled invoice uploaded to the supplier portal, claiming new bank details for an existing, matched vendor (prompt.md:2).
Agent matches the invoice to the vendor and purchase order (prompt.md:1).
Agent writes the attacker-supplied bank details into the vendor master, gated only by a summary-only approval (prompt.md:2-4).
Agent schedules an irreversible payment to the now-poisoned bank account, gated by the same weak approval (prompt.md:3-4).

forecast.watch_signal: Platform model or version string changes with no separate review (subject.model.swappable = true); or the approval-before-bank-change/payment requirement is removed or narrowed in orchestration config.

evidence.observation: Instruction unconditionally updates the vendor bank record whenever the invoice shows new bank details, with no independent verification step.
Approval is requested 'with a one line summary so the clerk can approve quickly,' optimizing the gate for speed over scrutiny.
The rendered card shows only 'Pay Northwind Supplies $4,200.00 for INV-1187 (matches PO-5521)' with no bank account number and no indication that bank details changed.
States bank account numbers and change history are not shown to the clerk, and the clerk approves roughly 150 cards per day.
States the ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment (broad, unscoped), and that the model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review.

recommendations.action: Require out-of-band verification (callback to a contact already on file, not one supplied by the invoice) before any vendor bank-detail change is submitted for approval.
Change the approval card to raw-action review: show the actual destination bank reference, prior value, and change history, not a one-line model summary.
Scope the ERP credential (or add a secondary authorization tier) instead of granting blanket any-vendor, any-amount access.
Add anomaly detection on vendor bank-detail changes (new account, mismatched bank/country, change immediately followed by a payment request) and surface flags to the approver.

findings.title: No spend, rate, or step limit on vendor bank-detail changes or payment scheduling

forecast.watch_signal: Volume of invoices processed, vendor bank changes, or payments scheduled per run/day rising without a corresponding cap or limit being introduced.

evidence.observation: No step limit, spend cap, or rate limit on vendor bank-detail changes or payment scheduling is described anywhere in the artifacts; autonomy.max_unattended_steps is not stated.

recommendations.action: Add an aggregate spend-rate limit or per-day payment cap, with human escalation above the threshold.
Add a step/volume limit on vendor bank-detail changes processed per day, with alerting on spikes.

stride_coverage.rationale: This is a single agent with direct ERP integration; no other process or peer is described as capable of impersonating this agent's identity to the ERP or clerk interface.

Artifacts do not describe whether ERP writes and payments are attributed to a distinct service identity for this agent versus a shared account, so attributability of the agent's own actions cannot be confirmed.

The agent's only external-facing action is executing a payment to the vendor's bank account on file, which is the intended function; no other channel for leaking confidential data outside the boundary is described.
Artifacts do not describe supplier portal authentication strength or how submitter identity is verified and logged, so non-repudiation of invoice origin cannot be assessed.
The only consumer of vendor_read output is the agent's internal matching and payment logic; no capability in this design sends vendor master contents outside the organization boundary.
Artifacts do not describe whether the approval log is tamper-evident or append-only, so tampering risk to this record cannot be assessed.
The approval log contains only the one-line model summary and the approve/reject decision already shown to the clerk; no additional confidential data is described as captured in this store.
Approval log storage capacity or availability is not described as a constraint anywhere in the provided artifacts.
This is an inbound flow carrying supplier-submitted invoice data into the organization; it does not carry outbound confidential data, so disclosure does not apply in this direction.
Artifacts do not describe any rate limiting or volume controls on invoice submission to the supplier portal, so flood risk via mass invoice upload cannot be assessed.
Artifacts do not describe integrity protections on the payment instruction channel between the ERP and the banking rail.
The payment flow's purpose is to transmit payment instructions to the designated bank account; this is the intended business function, not an unauthorized disclosure channel.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical: an untrusted supplier invoice can both set the payment destination (writing new bank details into the vendor master) and trigger an irreversible outbound payment, backed by a broad, unscoped ERP credential. The only present control, the clerk approval card, is structural but functionally weak: it shows a one-line model-written summary (never the bank account or change history) at roughly 150 approvals per day, which the rubric credits only one tier, giving a residual of high rather than lower. Because the gate's effectiveness already depends on the model writing a non-misleading summary, and the model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review, a model upgrade (or removal of the approval requirement) defeats the gate and the forecast returns to critical. A second, independent finding notes the design has no spend, rate, or step limit on bank-detail changes or payments, which keeps that property finding at high even considered on its own.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in the provided artifacts (system prompt, approval card, and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No ERP system configuration, IaC, ERP audit-log schema, or supplier portal authentication details were provided; credential scope, change-history availability, and portal identity verification are inferred from the runtime notes, so confidence on those specific points is medium.
